title: Partial Payments and the Cure Period of a Home-Site Lease Nonpayment Notice
content:
The cure period of a nonpayment notice on a Home-Site Lease is lengthened by a partial-payment extension, in days, read from the latest payment on the lease and the most recent rent charge.

**Desk rule.** The extension is 2 days when the latest payment, received on or after the due date of the most recent rent charge, is at least half of that period's rent and occupant charges less credits; 1 day when it is smaller; and none when no payment was received on or after that due date.

| Latest payment on the lease | Partial-payment extension |
|---|---|
| received on or after the due date of the most recent rent charge, at least half of that period's charges less credits | 2 days |
| received on or after that due date, smaller than that half | 1 day |
| none received on or after that due date | none |

**Points of judgement**

- The latest payment is the single most recent payment received on the lease. If it was received before the due date of the most recent rent charge, no payment counts as received on or after that due date.
- The half is measured against that one billing period's rent and occupant charges less its rent credits, not against the whole balance.

**Hypothetical period charges of 715.00 (half: 357.50)**

| Latest payment | Received | Extension |
|---|---|---|
| 400.00 | 6 days after the due date | 2 days |
| 357.50 | on the due date | 2 days |
| 120.00 | 9 days after the due date | 1 day |
| 700.00 | 3 days before the due date | none |
